knowledge:
- key_parameters: uniprot_id=The UniProt accession number of the target protein used in getProteinFeatures() ;; taxonomy_id=The taxonomy ID for the protein's species in getProteinFeatures() (defaults to human, ID: 9606) ;; start/end=The start and end residue positions of the immunogen in addImmunogen() ;; seq=The amino acid sequence of the immunogen in addImmunogen() (alternative to start/end) ;; name=The character string identifier for the immunogen used across adding, renaming, removing, plotting, and evaluating functions
- alternatives: None mentioned for the R workflow, but the documentation references the Antibodypedia database for identifying antibodies with known immunogen peptides, and external literature for comprehensive antibody validation.
- when_to_use: Use as a pre-selection step to exclude unsuitable antibodies early on when the immunogen sequence or position is known, particularly when evaluating whether an antibody raised against a peptide immunogen can successfully detect a natively folded protein.
- pitfalls: The length of an immunogen must be strictly between 10 and 50 amino acids ;; The default taxonomy ID in getProteinFeatures() is human (9606), so the correct taxonomy ID must be explicitly set for other species ;; The package is a pre-selection tool and does not replace comprehensive experimental antibody validation ;; In secondary structure predictions, "Other" usually stands for coil structures.

workflows.name: immunogen_evaluation_and_visualization
workflows.intent: Retrieve protein features, add candidate immunogens, visualize their positions, and evaluate their structural/functional properties to select the best antibody.
input: Immunogen coordinates (start and end integers) or peptide sequences (string)
workflows.stages: 1. Retrieve protein features from UniProt and PredictProtein using getProteinFeatures() ;; 2. Add candidate immunogens using addImmunogen() ;; 3. Rename or remove immunogens if necessary using renameImmunogen() or removeImmunogen() ;; 4. Plot the full protein sequence with annotated features and immunogens using plotProtein() ;; 5. Plot a detailed view of a specific immunogen using plotImmunogen() ;; 6. Generate a summary evaluation table of all immunogens using evaluateImmunogen()
workflows.code:
protein <- getProteinFeatures("Q9NZC2")
protein <- addImmunogen(protein, start = 142, end = 192, name = "ABIN2783734_")
protein <- addImmunogen(protein, start = 196, end = 230, name = "HPA010917")
protein <- addImmunogen(protein, seq = "HGQKPGTHPPSELD", name = "EB07921")
protein <- renameImmunogen(protein, oldName = "ABIN2783734_", newName = "ABIN2783734")
protein <- removeImmunogen(protein, name = "HPA010917")
plotProtein(protein)
plotImmunogen(protein, "ABIN2783734")
immunogens <- evaluateImmunogen(protein)
